findings.repro: Found by reading the code, not reproduced (it needs a write). Request A records a bank_transfer with slip S on lease L1. While A is still running (it has passed the storage.objects existence check in record_payment), request B from someone in the same org sends the same slipPath S on lease L2 with an amount over the cap. B gets 422 from record_payment. Its catch calls removeOrphanSlip, and the prisma.payments.findFirst({slip_path:S}) check cannot see A's uncommitted row, so B deletes S from Storage. A then commits a payment whose slip_path points to a file that no longer exists, which breaks R44 ('slip_path must point to an existing file'). The same path also lets any staff member delete another staff member's slip that is uploaded but not yet recorded, by sending a bad request that cites its path.
findings.fix: Only remove a slip that this request uploaded itself, or run the cleanup through a private plpgsql function that locks the slip's lease first, so in-flight recordings are serialized. A simpler option is a uniqueness claim on slip_path (for example, insert into a slip_claims table) taken before validation, so a concurrent second user of S fails without deleting it.

findings.repro: GET /api/reports/collections?from=2016-01&to=2026-12 (132 months) as manager@northwind.test gives 400 {error:'Invalid range'}, but the brief only defines an invalid range as a malformed one or from > to. The MAX_MONTHS = 120 limit is not in SPEC.md or DECISIONS.md (D25 does not mention it), so it is an unlogged decision.
findings.fix: Log the limit in DECISIONS.md as decided-by: pending and raise it (for example to 1200 months, which still bounds generate_series), or drop it. Add a test at the boundary.

findings.repro: The comment '-- D7: the cap is computed after the lease lock; READ COMMITTED gives each statement a fresh snapshot after the wait' was copied into lock_payment_for_manager, create_gateway_bill and apply_gateway_callback. None of these computes the cap, and apply_gateway_callback takes the bill lock before the lease lock. Someone reading the code during the walkthrough is misled at a lock-order decision point.
findings.fix: Give each copy a comment that matches its function. For example, in apply_gateway_callback: '-- D7: READ COMMITTED so the re-read after the bill lock wait sees the committed status'.

findings.repro: dates.ts keeps its own copies of daysInMonth, the leap-year rule and MYT_OFFSET_MS, which billing.ts already has (billing.ts:20, 22-29), even though dates.ts already re-exports from billing.ts. If one copy is changed and the other is not, input validation and schedule generation would disagree.
findings.fix: Export daysInMonth and MYT_OFFSET_MS from billing.ts (it stays pure) and import them in dates.ts.

findings.area: storage policies (R44: slips are read through short-lived signed URLs)
findings.repro: I logged in as staff@northwind.test with the publishable key and called POST /storage/v1/object/sign/payment-slips/c7652a64-.../40b7e5e7-....pdf with body {"expiresIn":315360000}. It returned 200, and the token's exp-iat is 315360000 s (10 years). A GET of that signed URL with no credentials then returned 200 and the file. So the client-side SELECT policy lets any staff member mint a slip URL that never really expires and that anyone can open, which goes around the server's 60 s getSlipUrl. Staff can still download slips directly, so an insider leak is possible either way. That is why this is minor.
findings.fix: Drop policy payment_slips_select. Keep only the INSERT policy: a Storage upload with upsert=false needs only INSERT. Slips are then read only through getSlipUrl (secret key, 60 s, path taken from the DB row). Update catalog.test.ts:319 and the positive-control read test in slips.test.ts:184 to match, and re-run the upload tests in slips.test.ts to confirm uploads still pass.

findings.area: Data API writes (R42: every other insert/update/delete must fail for everyone)
findings.repro: information_schema.role_table_grants shows service_role with DELETE, INSERT, UPDATE and TRUNCATE on all 10 public tables. These are Supabase's default grants and the migration never revokes them. With the secret key, PostgREST will therefore accept, for example, POST /rest/v1/memberships (privilege escalation), POST /rest/v1/leases (a lease with no invoices and no audit row), or PATCH /rest/v1/payments?id=eq.<pending> set status=approved (payments_guard allows that transition, so the payment is approved with no allocation and no audit). The app never writes through service_role: Prisma connects as postgres, and the admin client is used only for Auth admin and Storage. The secret key is server-only, so this is defence in depth only. audit_log is correctly protected: I confirmed UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE raise P0409 as service_role, as owner, and under session_replication_role=replica.
findings.fix: Add `revoke insert, update, delete, truncate on all tables in schema public from service_role;` (keep SELECT, which the Auth/Storage tooling may need). Also add `alter default privileges in schema public revoke insert, update, delete, truncate on tables from service_role;`. Then add a catalog test that service_role has no write privilege on public tables.
